name: amish-paste

description.preschool: Amish Paste tomatoes are big, heart-shaped red tomatoes that are very thick and meaty inside. They have hardly any watery seeds, which makes them perfect for cooking into thick, delicious pasta sauce. We grow lots of them so we can make jars and jars of sauce to eat all year.
description.elementary: Amish Paste is a large paste tomato variety originally grown by Amish farming communities. Its fruit is shaped like a big oxheart and weighs 6 to 8 ounces. Inside, the flesh is very dense with a tiny seed cavity and very little water — this means when you cook them into sauce, they thicken quickly without hours of simmering. At Oak Vista we grow 12 plants and aim to make about 90 quarts of Italian-style sauce each season.
description.secondary: Amish Paste is a paste/processing cultivar of Solanum lycopersicum characterised by large oxheart-shaped fruit (170–230 g), exceptionally low water content, and a small locular cavity relative to fruit volume. The dry matter content is high compared to San Marzano and Roma types, yielding thick sauce with minimal reduction time. The variety shows good general vigour and disease tolerance in hot Mediterranean climates. Seed provenance for the Oak Vista 2026 planting is unconfirmed — sourced from The Plant Barn, Chico CA, and may be a commercial hybrid rather than the true open-pollinated Amish heirloom. Breeding status flagged UNKNOWN pending verification.
description.university: Amish Paste — a large-fruited paste cultivar of Solanum lycopersicum, reportedly originating from Amish farming communities in Wisconsin. Fruit morphology: oxheart to elongated plum, 170–230 g, with high pericarp-to-locule ratio and low gel content. Brix values typically 5.0–5.5°, comparable to San Marzano but with superior sauce yield per unit fresh weight due to reduced aqueous fraction. Estimated production at Oak Vista: 15–20 lbs per plant under adequate calcium and consistent irrigation — critical given the very low soluble Ca (6.99 lbs/1000 sqft, FGL CH 2671853) and coco coir Ca²⁺ binding in the substrate. The 2026 planting (12 plants, ~300 sqft) targets 180–240 lbs total fresh weight yielding 72–96 quarts finished sauce at a 2.5 lb/quart conversion rate. Variety type requires verification from a certified seed source (Baker Creek Heirloom Seeds) before inclusion in any seed saving program.

gardenNotes: 12 plants in front raised beds, planted April 6, 2026. Evaluating as primary sauce variety for 90-quart annual production target. Confirm open-pollinated status before saving seed — source verified OP seeds from Baker Creek Heirloom Seeds (rareseeds.com) this fall if variety performs well.

name: italian-pear-nicks

description.preschool: Nick's Italian Pear tomato is a very special tomato that has been grown by the same family for over fifty years. The original grower saved seeds from the very best tomatoes every single year. Now we are growing them here in Chico and saving the seeds every single year so this special tomato is never lost.
description.elementary: Nick's Italian Pear is a true heirloom paste tomato that has been carefully grown and seed-saved for more than 50 years. Each year, the grower saved seeds from the best tomatoes — the ones that ripened earliest, produced the most fruit, and tasted the best. Over many decades this created a unique variety perfectly suited to California growing. The 2026 season at Oak Vista is the very first year these seeds are being grown in Chico, beginning a new chapter of adapting this irreplaceable family variety to Sacramento Valley conditions.
description.secondary: Italian Pear (Nick's) is a true open-pollinated heirloom paste tomato maintained through continuous seed selection for over 50 years in California. The variety produces traditional Italian pear-shaped fruit of medium size with excellent flavour developed through decades of selection for both fresh eating and sauce quality. The 2026 season at Oak Vista represents Generation 1 of the Chico climate adaptation selection program — seeds will be saved from the earliest-ripening, most productive, and best-flavoured fruit under Sacramento Valley conditions (100–110°F summer peaks, USDA Zone 9b). This variety carries SAVE_ANNUALLY seed saving policy without exception — the genetic heritage is irreplaceable.
description.university: Italian Pear (Nick's) — an open-pollinated paste cultivar of Solanum lycopersicum maintained through 50+ years of continuous phenotypic selection by a single cultivator in coastal California. The selection history represents a significant accumulation of locally adapted allele frequencies for Mediterranean climate performance — fruit quality, production timing, and disease tolerance traits shaped by half a century of directional selection pressure. The 2026 Oak Vista planting initiates a deliberate adaptation program to Sacramento Valley conditions: selection criteria target early ripening (critical under Chico's more extreme summer heat relative to coastal California's maritime moderation), high per-plant yield, and organoleptic quality for sauce production. This variety is modeled as a SeedLineage aggregate in the Naturalist application — the founding generation of Chico-adapted Italian Pear lineage. Seed saving protocol: fermentation extraction from the earliest-ripening, highest-yielding, best-flavoured fruit. Label with date, selection criteria, and generation number. Store in cool, dry conditions.

seedSource: Family heirloom — direct transfer, 50+ year selection history
gardenNotes: Front raised beds. Plant count TBD — update when final bed inventory completed. 2026 is first Chico season — monitor heat tolerance closely. HIGHEST PRIORITY seed lineage in the system. Save seeds from earliest ripening, highest production, best flavour fruit without exception.

name: sungold-cherry

description.preschool: Sungold is a little orange cherry tomato that is one of the sweetest things you can eat straight from the garden. The tiny fruits are like little orange jewels hanging in clusters, and they taste like candy made from sunshine. We grow just one plant and it makes hundreds and hundreds of little tomatoes.
description.elementary: Sungold is a cherry tomato variety that produces small, bright orange fruit with an incredibly sweet, complex flavour that many gardeners consider the best-tasting cherry tomato in the world. It is an F1 hybrid, which means its seeds will not grow true — each year you must buy new plants or seeds. The single plant at Oak Vista grows in the courtyard bed near the passion fruit vine, trained on a small trellis with companion zinnias and borage planted nearby for bee forage.
description.secondary: Sungold is an indeterminate F1 hybrid cherry tomato (Solanum lycopersicum) producing small orange fruit with exceptionally high sugar content and complex flavour combining sweetness with tropical fruit notes. The hybrid vigour (heterosis) contributes to prolific production from June through October in Chico conditions, with very good heat tolerance. As an F1 hybrid, saved seed will segregate in the F2 generation — do not save seed. The single plant at Oak Vista is grown in the courtyard bed adjacent to the Passiflora edulis trellis area, in E.B. Stone Planting Compost (bat guano, alfalfa meal, kelp meal) over native soil. Companion planted with zinnias and borage for pollinator support.
description.university: Sungold F1 — an indeterminate cherry cultivar of Solanum lycopersicum bred by Tokita Seed Company (Japan). Fruit: 15–20 g, orange (high β-carotene, lycopene present but masked by carotenoid profile), Brix 9–10° — among the highest sugar concentrations in commercially available tomato cultivars. The F1 heterosis provides vigorous vegetative growth, disease tolerance (Fusarium wilt races 1 and 2, Tobacco mosaic virus), and sustained production under high-temperature conditions. Training protocol: 1–2 main stems, regular lateral sucker removal; the indeterminate habit will outgrow small trellises and may require tip-pruning or cascade training. Companion planting with Borago officinalis (buzz pollination, nectar) and Zinnia elegans (generalist pollinator attraction) provides functional pollinator habitat adjacent to the Passiflora edulis trellis.

gardenNotes: 1 plant in courtyard bed adjacent to passiflora trellis area. E.B. Stone Planting Compost over native soil. Train to 1-2 main stems, pinch suckers regularly. Small portable trellis installed — expect to outgrow it. Companion planted with zinnias and borage for bee forage.

name: san-marzano-f2

description.preschool: These San Marzano tomato plants were grown from seeds we saved from last year's tomatoes. But those tomatoes were a special kind called a hybrid, so the babies might not look or taste like their parents — it is a surprise what they will do. Some of the plants are not feeling very well, so we are watching them carefully.
description.elementary: These San Marzano plants were grown from seeds saved from what turned out to be F1 hybrid tomatoes. When you save seeds from a hybrid, the next generation (called F2) is unpredictable — the plants can be tall or short, productive or not, and the fruit may taste different from the parent. Four of the weakest plants were already removed, and the three remaining plants are being observed for 2026 performance. We will not save seeds from these plants.
description.secondary: San Marzano F2 — plants grown from seed saved from probable F1 hybrid San Marzano-type fruit. F2 generation plants exhibit genetic segregation as the heterozygous F1 parental genotype recombines, producing variable phenotypes across the offspring population. The Oak Vista 2026 planting started with 7 plants; 4 were removed due to poor vigour (purple/anthocyanin colouring, leaf curl, etiolation stress consistent with genetic segregation or environmental stress during germination). The 3 remaining plants are being observed for production performance. Seed saving is not appropriate — these plants are genetically unpredictable and do not represent a stable variety.
description.university: San Marzano F2 — second filial generation from probable F1 hybrid parentage. The F2 segregation ratio for polygenic traits (fruit size, shape, sugar content, disease resistance, growth habit) produces a wide phenotypic distribution; the observed variable vigour and stress symptoms (anthocyanin accumulation, epinasty, etiolation) across the original 7-plant cohort are consistent with segregation rather than uniform environmental stress. The 4 culled individuals likely represent recombinant genotypes with reduced fitness under the specific growing conditions. The 3 retained plants may produce adequate fruit for fresh use but should not be evaluated as representative of the San Marzano type. If the San Marzano cultivar is desired for future seasons, source verified DOP-type seed from a reputable supplier (e.g. Seeds from Italy, Baker Creek) to obtain the true indeterminate paste type.

seedSource: Saved seed from prior season F1 hybrid fruit
gardenNotes: 3 remaining plants (4 weakest removed). Variable condition — some showing purple/anthocyanin colouring, leaf curl, etiolation stress. Observe 2026 performance. If poor producers, replace with verified heirloom seed source in 2027. Do not save seeds from these plants.

name: genovese-basil

description.preschool: Genovese basil has big, soft, dark-green leaves that smell like sweet pizza. We pinch off the tops to make them grow bushier, and we use the leaves for pesto and to put on top of fresh tomato salads. Bees and bumble bees love the tiny white flowers when we let some plants flower.
description.elementary: Genovese basil is the classic Italian cooking basil, prized for its large fragrant leaves perfect for pesto, caprese, and fresh tomato dishes. It is an open-pollinated heirloom variety, which means saving seeds from the best plants will produce more plants like them. At Oak Vista we are selecting plants that resist bolting (rushing to flower) under Chico's hot summers — basil normally flowers and stops making leaves when temperatures climb above 100°F.
description.secondary: Genovese basil is the Italian sweet basil chemotype of Ocimum basilicum, characterised by linalool-dominant essential oil chemistry that gives the variety its classic pesto-friendly aroma profile. The cultivar group is open-pollinated and amenable to mass selection — Oak Vista's Generation 1 lineage is selecting for delayed bolting under Sacramento Valley sustained-heat conditions while preserving leaf size and essential-oil intensity. Founding stock comes from Baker Creek Heirloom Seeds verified open-pollinated lines. Predominantly self-pollinating (cleistogamous flower structure) with 5–15% outcrossing rates, isolation requirements are modest — minimum 30 m separation from chemotypically distinct selections (Thai basil, lemon basil) is recommended to prevent linalool-pathway introgression that would dilute the Genovese chemotype.
description.university: Genovese — the canonical Italian sweet basil cultivar group within Ocimum basilicum var. basilicum, distinguished by linalool-dominant volatile profile (linalool typically 40–60% of essential oil, with 1,8-cineole, eugenol, and methyl eugenol as secondary constituents). Open-pollinated with stable inheritance under mass selection; Sacramento Valley adaptation program at Oak Vista targets elevated thermal thresholds for the ethylene-mediated bolting transition (target sustained tolerance to 38°C+ without floral induction) while monitoring chemotype drift via organoleptic panel and (eventually) GC-MS quantification of the linalool:methyleugenol ratio. The cleistogamous flower architecture limits but does not eliminate outcrossing; isolation distances of 30 m from chemotypically divergent O. basilicum stands are recommended for Generation-level chemotype preservation, with strict temporal isolation (staggered flowering, separated harvest) advisable in years where multiple basil chemotypes share a planting window.

seedSource: Baker Creek Heirloom Seeds (rareseeds.com) — verified open-pollinated Genovese.
gardenNotes: Kitchen garden. Generation 1 of Chico adaptation program. Pinch flower spikes weekly until the seed-saving cohort is selected late in the season; mark 5+ plants showing latest bolting and let those finish flowering and set seed. Save seed from at least 5 plants to preserve genetic diversity.

name: thai-basil

description.preschool: Thai basil smells a little like liquorice and has pretty purple flowers and stems. It handles hot weather even better than the green Italian basil. We use the leaves in stir fries, curries, and pho — they taste a bit spicy and sweet at the same time.
description.elementary: Thai basil (Ocimum basilicum var. thyrsiflora) is a different variety of the same basil species used for Italian cooking, but with a very different anise-liquorice flavour used in Southeast Asian dishes — stir fries, curries, and pho. It naturally handles heat better than Genovese because it evolved in tropical Southeast Asia. The purple flower spikes are heavily visited by carpenter bees at Oak Vista. We save seeds from the most aromatic, sturdiest plants and keep the planting separated from the Genovese basil so the two chemotypes do not cross.
description.secondary: Thai basil is the var. thyrsiflora variant of Ocimum basilicum, distinguished from sweet basil by its estragole-dominant essential oil profile (giving the characteristic anise-liquorice aroma) and by its higher inherent heat tolerance reflecting tropical Southeast Asian origin. At Oak Vista, the cultivar serves both culinary roles (Vietnamese, Thai, and Lao cuisines) and as a heavily visited carpenter bee (Xylocopa varipuncta) nectar source through its purple thyrsoid inflorescences. Selection focus at Generation 1 is aroma intensity, stem rigidity, and sustained vegetative production through the full Sacramento Valley summer. Chemotype isolation from Genovese is the key seed-saving constraint — minimum 30 m separation or staggered flowering windows are required to prevent linalool-pathway introgression that would compromise the estragole chemotype.
description.university: Thai basil — Ocimum basilicum var. thyrsiflora, the estragole (methyl chavicol) dominant chemotype within the species, with estragole typically 60–80% of total volatile fraction and characteristic accessory profile of methyl eugenol and (Z)-ocimene. Open-pollinated, amenable to mass selection on the same self-pollinating, low-outcrossing genetic architecture as Genovese sweet basil — but with the additional constraint that the chemotype boundary between estragole-dominant (Thai) and linalool-dominant (Genovese) selections is mediated by simple-inheritance loci in the eugenol O-methyltransferase pathway. Outcrossing between chemotypes within the recommended 30 m isolation distance can introgress linalool-pathway alleles into the Thai estragole background within a single generation, so temporal isolation (staggered flowering) is advisable in years where both chemotypes share a planting window. Tropical (likely Indochinese) center of diversity confers pre-adaptation to sustained high temperatures, with photosynthetic optimum well above the species mean.

seedSource: Local nursery start (variety confirmed by floral morphology and aroma profile).
gardenNotes: Kitchen garden. Generation 1 of Chico adaptation program. Maintain minimum 30 m isolation from Genovese basil planting, or stagger flowering by pinching one cohort while letting the other set seed. Higher inherent heat tolerance than Genovese — fewer bolt-resistance management interventions needed.

name: italian-flat-leaf-parsley

description.preschool: Italian parsley has flat, dark green leaves that taste fresh and a little peppery. We add it to soups, salads, and pasta. The plants live two whole years — the second year they grow tall flower stalks that beneficial insects love to visit.
description.elementary: Italian flat-leaf parsley (Petroselinum crispum var. neapolitanum) is the traditional Mediterranean cooking parsley, with broader, flatter, and stronger-flavoured leaves than the curly-leaf form. It is biennial — the first year produces the harvestable rosette of leaves; the second year, the plant bolts into tall umbels of tiny white flowers that attract parasitic wasps and hoverflies, both of which help control aphids on the tomatoes. We let some plants overwinter into year two for both the beneficial insect support and to harvest seeds.
description.secondary: Italian flat-leaf parsley is the var. neapolitanum cultivar group of Petroselinum crispum, preferred over var. crispum (curled parsley) for both organoleptic quality (stronger and cleaner flavour driven by the characteristic petroselinic acid and myristicin profile) and visual presentation in Mediterranean cuisine. Biennial life cycle requires vernalisation for second-year bolting — Chico's mild winters (~800 chill hours, USDA Zone 9b) reliably trigger the transition without killing the plant. As an obligate outcrosser (protandrous Apiaceae umbels enforce cross-pollination), seed saving requires minimum 10+ plants for adequate genetic diversity and minimum 400 m isolation from var. crispum to maintain the flat-leaf chemotype.
description.university: Petroselinum crispum var. neapolitanum — the flat-leaf Mediterranean parsley cultivar group, distinguished from var. crispum by deeply trifoliate planar leaflet morphology, more robust petiole architecture, and elevated essential-oil intensity (myristicin and apiol concentrations approximately 1.5–2× those of curled-leaf forms in foliar tissue). Biennial obligate outcrosser with protandrous Apiaceae umbel architecture; minimum effective seed-saving population sizes are 10+ plants, with isolation distances of 400 m from var. crispum required to preserve the flat-leaf morphological and chemotypic identity. The 2-year generation time halves the rate of response to selection compared with annual culinary herbs — adaptation programs require correspondingly extended timelines and continuous record-keeping across overwintering cohorts. Apiaceae seed viability declines rapidly post-harvest (typically usable within 1–2 years), making annual seed harvest a hard constraint rather than an option.

seedSource: Baker Creek Heirloom Seeds verified open-pollinated Italian Giant.
gardenNotes: Kitchen garden. Biennial — Chico Zone 9b winters provide adequate vernalisation. Maintain 10+ plants for seed-saving genetic diversity. Mark best vegetative plants in year one for overwintering into year two seed harvest. Isolate 400 m from any curled-leaf parsley plantings (no curled parsley currently at Oak Vista).

name: black-beauty-eggplant

description.preschool: Black Beauty eggplants are big, shiny, dark purple fruits that grow on bushy plants. They love hot weather, so Chico summers are perfect for them. We slice them up and grill them, or bake them into eggplant parmesan.
description.elementary: Black Beauty is one of the oldest eggplant varieties — it has been grown since 1902, before most modern hybrid vegetables existed. It produces large, glossy, dark purple fruits perfect for grilling, baking, and making eggplant parmesan. Eggplant flea beetles chew tiny pinholes in the leaves but the plants usually outgrow the damage. We save seeds from the biggest, glossiest fruits on the healthiest plants, scooping out the tiny flat seeds and drying them for next year's planting.
description.secondary: Black Beauty is an heirloom open-pollinated cultivar of Solanum melongena introduced in 1902, predating modern hybrid breeding. As a Solanaceae member, eggplant is predominantly self-pollinating but with 5–20% outcrossing rates (higher than tomato due to larger, more accessible floral structure) mediated by Bombus and Xylocopa visitation — minimum 50 m isolation from other S. melongena cultivars is recommended for clean seed saving. Selection at Chico targets fruit yield, glossy skin quality (anthocyanin concentration in the exocarp), tolerance to Epitrix hirtipennis (eggplant flea beetle) feeding damage, and quantitative resistance to Verticillium dahliae race 1 — the predominant Sacramento Valley soilborne pathogen of Solanaceae.
description.university: Black Beauty — heirloom open-pollinated Solanum melongena cultivar, introduced 1902. Represents a pre-Green Revolution gene pool maintained through over a century of open-pollinated propagation across multiple seed companies and home gardeners; phenotypic stability across this lineage is high, indicating well-fixed major-gene control of fruit morphology (round-to-pyriform shape, 150–250 g fruits) and exocarp anthocyanin chemistry (nasunin-dominant profile). The 5–20% outcrossing rate (Bombus and Xylocopa-mediated) is sufficient to maintain heterozygosity but low enough to permit mass selection without strict isolation; 50 m separation from other S. melongena cultivars preserves the Black Beauty phenotype. Key selection targets at Oak Vista: quantitative resistance to Verticillium dahliae race 1 (predominant Sacramento Valley pathotype, available across long-cultivated heirloom backgrounds), reduced Epitrix hirtipennis feeding preference (trichome density and foliar glycoalkaloid concentration are the candidate resistance mechanisms), and sustained fruit set through the full Chico summer thermal regime (40°C+ peaks).

seedSource: Certified organic nursery starts; verified heirloom open-pollinated Black Beauty.
gardenNotes: Kitchen garden. Generation 1 of Chico adaptation. Eggplant excels in Sacramento Valley heat — among the few Solanaceae that improves with extreme temperatures. Flea beetle management is the primary production challenge — row-cover during early establishment recommended. Save seed from 3+ plants minimum, harvesting from overripe fruit left on the plant until the skin turns dull brown-yellow.
